issues.sym: A ticking sound, loudest on a cold start, that may fade as the engine warms up. You may smell exhaust under the hood or in the cabin.
issues.why: Repeated heating and cooling makes the manifold flex until the bolts, usually at the rear of the head, snap. Exhaust then leaks past the gasket. It is often mistaken for lifter tick.
issues.next: Have the manifold bolts inspected. Get the leak fixed soon if you smell exhaust inside the car.

issues.t: HEMI lifter tick and camshaft wear
issues.sym: A ticking or metallic chirp that stays or grows louder once warm, sometimes with misfires and a check engine light.
issues.why: The needle bearings in a roller lifter can seize, so the lifter grinds against the camshaft and flattens the lobe. Metal from the damage spreads through the oil.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed promptly and limit driving until you know the cause. Caught early, the fix is lifters and camshaft; ignored, it can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Left cylinder head valve seat wear (3.6L)
issues.sym: Check engine light with a misfire, most often on cylinder 2, plus rough running, a ticking noise, and lost power.
issues.why: Valve seats and guides in the left cylinder head on early engines could overheat and wear, so the cylinder lost compression. Chrysler revised the head and extended warranty coverage on it.
issues.next: Have the misfire checked with a compression or leak-down test. Ask a dealer whether the extended coverage still applies to your car.

issues.sym: The battery light comes on, lights dim, steering can get heavy, and the engine may stall and not restart.
issues.why: The alternator could fail internally without warning. On cars with electro-hydraulic power steering, losing charging power can also cut steering assist. Chrysler recalled these cars more than once.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the battery light comes on, get off the road safely and have the charging system checked before driving further.

issues.sym: Oil or coolant pooling on top of the engine or dripping at the back, a burning smell, or oil or coolant loss between changes.
issues.why: The oil filter and cooler housing is plastic and sits in the valley under the intake. Heat cycling can warp or crack it, and its seals harden and leak.
issues.next: Have the leak source confirmed and the housing or seals replaced. Keep an eye on oil and coolant levels until it is fixed.

issues.sym: A ticking from the top of the engine, sometimes with a misfire code and check engine light.
issues.why: The rocker arms that ride on the camshaft can wear or fail. Chrysler released a revised part, but newer engines still have the problem.
issues.next: Have the noise and any misfire diagnosed. Repairs mean replacing the rocker arms and sometimes the lifters or camshaft.

issues.t: Loose front driveshaft bolts on AWD (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or vibration from the front of the car. If the shaft comes loose, the car can lose drive or roll while in Park unless the parking brake is set.
issues.why: Bolts holding the front driveshaft on some all-wheel-drive cars could work loose. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Use the parking brake when parked and have any new clunk checked before driving further.

issues.t: Cruise control may not turn off (recall)
issues.sym: Cruise control stays on and the car keeps accelerating or holding speed after you try to cancel it.
issues.why: An electrical short while cruise control is active could stop the system from switching off. Chrysler recalled millions of vehicles, including these, for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If it ever happens, brake firmly and shift to Neutral to stop the car.

issues.t: Side curtain air bag inflators can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no warning before a crash. An air bag warning light is not a reliable sign.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect could make the side curtain air bag inflators break apart when they go off and throw metal pieces toward the people inside. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and get the repair done as soon as parts are available.

issues.t: Oil sludge and internal coolant leak can ruin the engine (2.7L)
issues.sym: Oil pressure light, ticking or knocking, running hot, milky or thick oil, and in bad cases sudden engine seizure.
issues.why: The 2.7L V6 runs hot and is prone to sludge, linked to its crankcase ventilation and small oil capacity. Its water pump is driven by the timing chain inside the engine, so when its gasket fails coolant leaks into the oil. Owners and class-action suits reported complete engine failures.
issues.next: Change oil on time with the correct oil. If the oil light comes on, you hear knocking, or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have the engine checked right away.

issues.t: Worn front tension struts, ball joints and tie rods
issues.sym: Clunking or banging over bumps, shaking over expansion joints, pulling to one side, alignment that will not stay set, and uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The front suspension wears its tension strut (compression arm) bushings and ball joints early, and owners also report tie rod ends and struts needing replacement.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and the worn parts replaced, then get an alignment. Replace a loose ball joint or tension strut promptly because it affects steering control.

issues.t: Car can roll away if not fully in Park (shifter recall)
issues.sym: The electronic gear selector springs back to center, so it is easy to think the car is in Park when it is still in gear. The car can move after the driver gets out.
issues.why: Cars with the eight-speed automatic and electronic shifter did not warn the driver well enough when the door opened with the car out of Park. Chrysler recalled them for a software update to reduce the risk of rollaway.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-240 (Chrysler S27). Until it is done, always confirm P on the dash and set the parking brake before getting out.
